event: The fall of the Berlin Wall
note: A garbled announcement that East Germans could travel freely sent crowds to the checkpoints, and by midnight the guards had opened them. The mark is the Brandenburg Gate, where the Wall became the night's stage.
Parisian crowds stormed the royal fortress-prison to seize its gunpowder, freeing the seven prisoners inside. Its site is now the Place de la Bastille.
The fire began in Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane and burned for four days, destroying some 13,200 houses and old St Paul's Cathedral.

event: President John F. Kennedy is assassinated
note: Kennedy was shot from the sixth floor of the Texas School Book Depository as his open-top motorcade passed through Dealey Plaza in Dallas.
The uranium bomb 'Little Boy' exploded about 600 m above the city centre, near what is now the Atomic Bomb Dome; some 70,000–80,000 people were killed outright.

event: The Titanic sinks on her maiden voyage
note: The liner struck an iceberg about 600 km south-south-east of Newfoundland and sank in under three hours; more than 1,500 people died. The wreck was found in 1985, 3,800 m down.

event: The Declaration of Independence is adopted
note: The Second Continental Congress adopted the Declaration in the Pennsylvania State House, now Independence Hall, in Philadelphia.
On the Ides of March, senators stabbed Caesar 23 times in the Curia of Pompey, whose remains lie in the Largo di Torre Argentina in Rome.
About 156,000 Allied troops came ashore on five beaches between the Cotentin peninsula and the mouth of the Orne in Normandy, opening a second front in western Europe.
Japanese carrier aircraft struck the US Pacific Fleet at its base on Oahu, damaging all eight battleships and killing 2,403 Americans; the US declared war the next day.
A botched safety test blew apart Reactor No. 4 and spread radioactive fallout across Europe. The nearby city of Pripyat was evacuated and has stood empty ever since.
Students and workers occupied the vast square in central Beijing for seven weeks; on the night of 3–4 June the army cleared it, killing hundreds or perhaps thousands in the surrounding streets.
Built as the tomb of the pharaoh Khufu on the Giza plateau, it was the tallest structure on Earth for more than 3,800 years.
The emperor Shah Jahan built the white marble mausoleum beside the Yamuna for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in childbirth in 1631.
The Inca citadel, probably an estate for the emperor Pachacuti, sits on a ridge high above the Urubamba valley in the Andes of Peru. It was abandoned around the time of the Spanish conquest.
Jørn Utzon's sail-roofed opera house on Bennelong Point in Sydney Harbour was opened by Elizabeth II after 14 years of building and huge cost overruns.

event: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated
note: France's gift to the United States, designed by Bartholdi with a frame by Gustave Eiffel, was dedicated on Bedloe's Island (now Liberty Island) in New York Harbor.

event: The Bolsheviks storm the Winter Palace
note: Red Guards took the Winter Palace in Petrograd, seat of the Provisional Government, with little resistance: the climax of the October Revolution (25 October in the old calendar).
Sultan Mehmed II's army broke through the land walls after a 53-day siege, ending the Byzantine Empire; the last emperor, Constantine XI, died in the fighting.

event: The first modern Olympic Games open
note: The first Games of the modern era were held in the marble Panathenaic Stadium in Athens, rebuilt on its ancient site. Spyridon Louis, a Greek water-carrier, won the first marathon.
After 27 years in prison, Mandela walked out of Victor Verster Prison near Paarl, then spoke to a huge crowd from the balcony of Cape Town City Hall that evening.
William of Normandy defeated Harold II on a ridge about 10 km inland from Hastings, where the town of Battle and its abbey now stand.
Gandhi was shot by the Hindu nationalist Nathuram Godse on his way to an evening prayer meeting in the garden of Birla House, New Delhi.

event: Hillary and Tenzing reach the summit of Everest
note: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first known climbers to stand on the world's highest summit, reached by the South Col route from Nepal.
The SS Ancon made the first official transit of the 82 km canal across the Isthmus of Panama, sparing ships the long voyage around South America.
The Red Army encircled and destroyed the German Sixth Army in the ruins of the city on the Volga, a turning point of the war in Europe. The hill of Mamayev Kurgan was fought over for months.

event: The Treaty of Versailles is signed
note: Germany and the Allies signed the peace in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles, the room where the German Empire had been proclaimed in 1871.
Colonists protesting the Tea Act boarded three ships at Griffin's Wharf and dumped 342 chests of East India Company tea into Boston Harbor.

event: Britain hands Hong Kong back to China
note: The handover ceremony was held at midnight in the new Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai, ending 156 years of British rule.
The 30 m Art Deco statue was consecrated on the summit of Corcovado, 700 m above Rio de Janeiro.
The emperor Titus opened the Flavian Amphitheatre in Rome with 100 days of games; it could hold perhaps 50,000 spectators.
Napoleon's Grande Armée marched into an almost deserted Moscow; fires soon destroyed much of the city, and five weeks later he began his disastrous retreat.

event: The first Olympic Games in Asia open
note: The Tokyo Games opened at the National Stadium, showcasing Japan's recovery from the war; the first bullet train had begun running nine days earlier.
Muhammad's army entered Mecca almost without bloodshed; he cleared the Kaaba of idols and the city became the holiest site of Islam.
Alexander laid out his new city on the Mediterranean coast of Egypt; under the Ptolemies it became home to the great Library and the Pharos lighthouse.
The 164 km canal joining the Mediterranean and the Red Sea opened with a ceremony at Port Said, attended by the Empress Eugénie of France.

event: Anne Frank's family goes into hiding
note: The Franks hid in a secret annexe behind Otto Frank's business on the Prinsengracht for two years, where Anne kept her diary, until they were betrayed in August 1944.

event: Fidel Castro enters Havana in triumph
note: After the dictator Batista fled on New Year's Day, Castro crossed the island in a week-long victory caravan and entered Havana to cheering crowds.
The temple to Athena on the Acropolis was finished under Pericles as a showpiece of Athenian power, its sculptures overseen by Phidias.

event: Martin Luther King Jr. says "I have a dream"
note: King spoke from the steps of the Lincoln Memorial to some 250,000 people at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom.
Ash and pumice entombed Pompeii and Herculaneum on the Bay of Naples. Pliny the Younger watched from Misenum across the bay and wrote the only eyewitness account.
Gavrilo Princip shot the heir to Austria-Hungary and his wife Sophie by the Latin Bridge in Sarajevo; within weeks Europe was at war.
The second atomic bomb, aimed at the city centre, exploded over the Urakami valley; about 40,000 people died instantly, and Japan announced its surrender six days later.

event: The Wright brothers make the first powered flight
note: Orville Wright flew 37 m in 12 seconds from the sand dunes at Kill Devil Hills near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina: the first controlled, sustained powered flight.

Lee's invasion of the North was turned back over three days in southern Pennsylvania, ending with the failed Pickett's Charge. Lincoln gave his Gettysburg Address at the battlefield cemetery that November.

event: Martin Luther publishes his Ninety-five Theses
note: Luther's attack on the sale of indulgences, traditionally nailed to the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg, sparked the Protestant Reformation.
Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Emperor of the Romans at Christmas Mass in Old St Peter's Basilica, reviving the imperial title in the West.
The crusaders stormed Jerusalem after a five-week siege and massacred much of its population, founding a kingdom that held the city for 88 years.
Hernán Cortés and his Tlaxcalan allies took the island city in Lake Texcoco after a siege of almost three months; Mexico City was built on its ruins.

event: The Mayflower Pilgrims found Plymouth Colony
note: After first anchoring off Cape Cod, the Pilgrims settled at Plymouth in Massachusetts, where about half of them died in the first winter.

event: The great sarsen stones of Stonehenge are raised
note: The sarsen circle and trilithons were raised on Salisbury Plain around 2500 BC, aligned on the midsummer sunrise and the midwinter sunset.
Carter uncovered the steps to the boy king's almost intact tomb in the Valley of the Kings, on the west bank of the Nile opposite Luxor.

event: Japan signs its surrender aboard USS Missouri
note: Japan's foreign minister and army chief signed the Instrument of Surrender on the deck of the US battleship anchored in Tokyo Bay, formally ending the Second World War.

event: The Battle of the Somme begins
note: On the first day of the Anglo-French offensive in Picardy the British Army suffered 57,000 casualties, its worst single day; the battle dragged on until November.

Irish republicans seized the General Post Office in Dublin and proclaimed an Irish Republic; the rising was crushed within a week, but the executions of its leaders swung opinion towards independence.

event: The Congress of Vienna redraws Europe
note: Europe's statesmen remade the continent after Napoleon's defeat, meeting at the Austrian chancellery on the Ballhausplatz under Metternich amid a famous round of balls.

Guided by Makololo boatmen, the Scottish missionary viewed the great falls of the Zambezi, known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders', from an island on their lip and named them after his queen.
An earthquake centred in the Atlantic off south-west Portugal, followed by a tsunami and fires, flattened much of Lisbon on All Saints' Day and killed tens of thousands.

event: Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated
note: King was shot on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, where he had come to support striking sanitation workers; the motel is now the National Civil Rights Museum.
Hours after the last US helicopters left, a North Vietnamese tank crashed through the gates of the Independence Palace, ending the Vietnam War.
The earthquake, centred just offshore, and the fires that followed destroyed about 80% of San Francisco; around 3,000 people died.
Khomeini flew home from Paris to a welcome from millions in Tehran; within ten days the Shah's last government had collapsed.
The volcano in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra blew itself apart; the explosion was heard 4,800 km away, and its tsunamis killed some 36,000 people.
Santa Anna's Mexican army stormed the old mission held by Texian rebels in San Antonio, killing nearly all its defenders, among them Davy Crockett and Jim Bowie.
Soviet soldiers reached the largest Nazi death camp, beside the Polish town of Oświęcim, and found about 7,000 prisoners still alive; some 1.1 million people had been murdered there.
Leonidas of Sparta and a small Greek force held the narrow coastal pass against Xerxes' Persian army for three days before being outflanked. Silt has since pushed the coastline kilometres away.
Built for the Khmer king Suryavarman II as a temple to Vishnu, near modern Siem Reap in Cambodia, it is the largest religious monument in the world.

event: China's first emperor is buried with the Terracotta Army
note: Some 8,000 life-size clay soldiers were buried in pits beside the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, east of modern Xi'an; farmers digging a well found them in 1974.

event: The Hijra: Muhammad leaves Mecca for a new home
note: Muhammad and his followers moved from Mecca to the oasis city of Yathrib, renamed Medina; the year of the Hijra became year one of the Islamic calendar.
Australian and New Zealand soldiers came ashore at a narrow cove on the Gallipoli peninsula, beginning an eight-month campaign that failed to force open the Dardanelles.
More than 338,000 British and French troops were taken off the harbour mole and beaches of Dunkirk, many by a flotilla of small civilian boats.
Kwame Nkrumah declared the Gold Coast independent as Ghana at midnight on the Old Polo Ground in Accra, where his memorial park now stands.

event: Charles Darwin explores the Galápagos Islands
note: HMS Beagle spent five weeks among the volcanic islands, about 900 km off Ecuador; their finches and giant tortoises later helped Darwin towards his theory of natural selection.

event: The moai of Easter Island are carved
note: Nearly all of Rapa Nui's almost 1,000 moai were carved from the soft volcanic tuff of the Rano Raraku crater, then moved across the island, perhaps 'walked' upright with ropes.

event: Brasília becomes the capital of Brazil
note: Brazil moved its capital from Rio de Janeiro to a new city on the central plateau, laid out by Lúcio Costa with buildings by Oscar Niemeyer, built in under four years.

event: Muhammad Ali wins the "Rumble in the Jungle"
note: Ali regained the world heavyweight title by knocking out George Foreman in the eighth round at the 20th of May Stadium in Kinshasa, in what was then Zaire.

event: Soviet tanks crush the Prague Spring
note: Warsaw Pact armies invaded Czechoslovakia to halt the reforms of the Prague Spring; crowds confronted the tanks in Wenceslas Square.
Methyl isocyanate gas leaked from the Union Carbide pesticide plant over the sleeping city of Bhopal; thousands died within days in the world's worst industrial disaster.

event: Stamford Raffles founds a British trading post
note: Raffles signed a treaty with the Sultan of Johor allowing the East India Company to set up a post at the mouth of the Singapore River, the start of modern Singapore.

event: The State of Israel is proclaimed
note: David Ben-Gurion read the declaration of independence in the Tel Aviv Museum, hours before the British Mandate expired; neighbouring Arab states invaded the next day.
Wellington's allied army and Blücher's Prussians defeated Napoleon on the ridges about 15 km south of Brussels, ending the Hundred Days. The Lion's Mound now marks the field.

event: Christopher Columbus makes landfall in the Americas
note: Columbus's first landfall was an island the Lucayans called Guanahani. Most historians identify it with San Salvador in the Bahamas, though Samana Cay and others have been proposed.
Athenian and Plataean hoplites routed a Persian landing force on the coastal plain of Marathon, north-east of Athens; the 192 Athenian dead were buried in the mound that still stands on the field.
Henry V's outnumbered and largely archer army defeated the French nobility on muddy fields between the woods of Azincourt and Tramecourt in northern France.
Nelson's fleet destroyed the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar in south-west Spain, ending Napoleon's hopes of invading Britain; Nelson was killed by a French marksman.

event: The Battle of the Little Bighorn
note: Lakota, Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors wiped out Custer's battalion of the 7th Cavalry on the ridges above the Little Bighorn River in Montana.
The north face of the volcano in Washington State collapsed in the largest landslide ever recorded, unleashing a sideways blast that flattened 600 km² of forest; 57 people died.

event: French soldiers find the Rosetta Stone
note: Troops rebuilding a fort near the Nile port of Rashid (Rosetta) found the stone, whose decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek became the key to reading hieroglyphs.
A German torpedo sank the Cunard liner off the Old Head of Kinsale in southern Ireland; 1,198 people died, 128 of them Americans, hardening US opinion against Germany.

event: Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin meet at Yalta
note: The Allied leaders met at the tsars' former summer palace of Livadia in Crimea to plan the defeat of Germany and the shape of post-war Europe.

event: Joan of Arc is burned at the stake
note: Captured by the Burgundians and convicted of heresy by a pro-English church court, Joan was burned in the old market square of Rouen, aged about 19.

event: Samuel de Champlain founds a settlement on the St Lawrence
note: Champlain built his 'Habitation' below the cliffs where the St Lawrence narrows, founding Quebec, the first permanent settlement of New France.
On the banks of the Ipiranga brook, then just outside São Paulo, the Portuguese prince regent cried 'Independence or death!' and became Brazil's first emperor.
About 1,400 CIA-trained Cuban exiles landed on Cuba's south coast; Castro's forces defeated them around Playa Girón within three days.

event: Shipyard strikers win the right to found Solidarity
note: A strike at the Lenin Shipyard in Gdańsk, led by the electrician Lech Wałęsa, won the right to form Solidarity, the first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc.
The Duke of Cumberland's army crushed Charles Edward Stuart's Jacobites on Drummossie Moor east of Inverness in under an hour: the last pitched battle on British soil.

event: Chile's presidential palace is bombed in Pinochet's coup
note: Air force jets rocketed La Moneda palace in central Santiago as the armed forces seized power; President Salvador Allende died inside, and General Pinochet ruled for 17 years.
Napoleon lured the Russian and Austrian emperors into attacking his weakened right, then seized the Pratzen Heights at the centre of their line, east of Brno in Moravia.

The longest battle of the First World War was fought around the forts north of Verdun; about 300,000 French and German soldiers died. The Douaumont ossuary holds the bones of 130,000 unidentified men.

event: The Second Battle of El Alamein
note: Montgomery's Eighth Army broke through Rommel's lines between the coast and the Qattara Depression, about 100 km west of Alexandria, turning the war in North Africa.
US carrier aircraft sank four Japanese carriers north-west of Midway Atoll, a remote US base about 2,100 km from Hawaii, turning the tide of the Pacific war.

event: US Marines raise the flag over Iwo Jima
note: Joe Rosenthal's photograph of Marines raising the flag on Mount Suribachi, the volcanic island's highest point, became the most reproduced image of the war; the battle lasted five weeks.

event: The Battle of Dien Bien Phu
note: The Viet Minh hauled artillery onto the hills around a French fortified valley in north-west Vietnam and forced its surrender, ending French rule in Indochina.

event: James Cook's Endeavour lands at Botany Bay
note: Cook anchored in a bay he named for the plants his naturalists collected there; the landing at Kurnell was the first British contact with Aboriginal people on Australia's east coast.

event: The Treaty of Waitangi is signed
note: More than 40 Māori chiefs signed the treaty with the British Crown on the lawn at Waitangi in the Bay of Islands; its English and Māori texts differ, and it remains New Zealand's founding document.

event: German and Italian aircraft bomb Guernica
note: Planes supporting Franco bombed the Basque market town for three hours; Picasso's painting made it a lasting symbol of the horror of war.
Trapped on the York River peninsula in Virginia by Washington's army and a French fleet, Cornwallis surrendered, effectively ending the American War of Independence.

event: The Romans take the fortress of Masada
note: The Tenth Legion built a huge ramp up the desert mesa above the Dead Sea to take Herod's fortress; according to Josephus, its Jewish defenders chose death over capture.
A pyroclastic flow engulfed Saint-Pierre, then the largest town in Martinique, killing about 28,000 people; a prisoner in a thick-walled cell was among the few survivors.

event: British and French troops burn the Old Summer Palace
note: At the end of the Second Opium War, troops looted and then burned the emperors' vast gardens of Yuanmingyuan, north-west of Beijing, in reprisal for the torture of envoys.

event: Thomas Becket is murdered in his cathedral
note: Four knights who took Henry II's angry words as an order killed the archbishop in Canterbury Cathedral; he was made a saint within three years.

event: Bedouin shepherds find the Dead Sea Scrolls
note: The first scrolls came from caves near Qumran, above the north-west shore of the Dead Sea; they include the oldest known manuscripts of the Hebrew Bible.

event: The Korean War armistice is signed
note: The armistice was signed at Panmunjom on the front line near the 38th parallel; no peace treaty followed, and the demilitarised zone still divides Korea.

event: The last Muslim kingdom in Spain surrenders
note: Muhammad XII (Boabdil) handed the Alhambra and the city of Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella, ending almost eight centuries of Muslim rule in Iberia.

event: Gandhi's Salt March reaches the sea
note: After 24 days and about 390 km on foot, Gandhi reached the coastal village of Dandi in Gujarat and picked up a lump of natural salt in defiance of the British salt tax.

Troops under Brigadier-General Dyer fired without warning on a crowd in the walled Jallianwala Bagh garden near the Golden Temple, killing at least 379 people by the official count, many more by others.
The Virginia Company's settlers built a fort on a marshy island in the James River: the first permanent English settlement in the Americas, where most died in the first years.
Alexander died aged 32 in Nebuchadnezzar's palace at Babylon, on the Euphrates south of modern Baghdad, after a sudden fever; his empire soon split among his generals.

event: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant
note: Barnard's team at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town gave Louis Washkansky the heart of a young road-accident victim; he lived for 18 days.
After a three-year siege, Scipio Aemilianus's army stormed and razed the city near modern Tunis, ending the Third Punic War; Rome later refounded it as a colony.
The charter was agreed at Runnymede, a Thames-side meadow between Windsor and Staines where the rebel barons met the king on neutral ground. The exact spot is unknown.
Hannibal's outnumbered army enveloped and destroyed eight Roman legions on the plain of the Aufidus (Ofanto) in Apulia, one of the bloodiest days in history; the exact field is debated.
Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeated Antony and Cleopatra off the mouth of the Ambracian Gulf in western Greece; their flight to Egypt left Octavian master of the Roman world.
Themistocles lured Xerxes' larger fleet into the narrow channel between the island of Salamis and the coast of Attica, where the Greek triremes routed it.

The galleys of the Holy League under Don John of Austria destroyed the Ottoman fleet off the Echinades islands at the mouth of the Gulf of Patras; Cervantes lost the use of his left hand in the fight.

event: The Charge of the Light Brigade
note: Through a misunderstood order, about 670 British light cavalry charged Russian guns down the North Valley near Balaklava in Crimea; nearly half were killed, wounded or captured.
William III defeated James II at a ford of the River Boyne near Drogheda, securing the Protestant succession; Ulster's Orangemen still mark it each July.
Charles Martel's Franks stopped an Umayyad army somewhere between Poitiers and Tours, traditionally at Moussais-la-Bataille; the exact site, and even the year, are disputed.

event: The Black Death reaches Sicily aboard Genoese galleys
note: Ships from the Black Sea brought plague into the harbour of Messina; within four years the Black Death had killed perhaps a third of Europe's people.

event: Gold is found at Sutter's Mill
note: James Marshall spotted gold flakes in the tailrace of a sawmill he was building for John Sutter on the South Fork of the American River, setting off the California Gold Rush.
Soviet tank armies clashed head-on with the II SS Panzer Corps near the village of Prokhorovka at the height of the Battle of Kursk, among the largest tank battles in history.
US Marines landed at Wolmido island and the port of Incheon, far behind North Korean lines and despite huge tides; Seoul was retaken within two weeks.
Tokugawa Ieyasu's victory in a mountain valley in central Japan, helped by defections from the enemy army, opened 250 years of rule by the Tokugawa shoguns.

event: Commodore Perry's black ships arrive in Japan
note: Perry's four warships anchored off Uraga at the mouth of Edo Bay and demanded that Japan open its ports, ending more than two centuries of seclusion.
Police opened fire on a crowd protesting the pass laws outside the police station in Sharpeville township, south of Johannesburg, killing 69 people.
Police fired on schoolchildren marching against compulsory teaching in Afrikaans; 12-year-old Hector Pieterson became the symbol of a rising that spread across South Africa.
The Ottomans under Murad I fought a Serbian-led army on the Field of Blackbirds, just north-west of Pristina; both rulers were killed, and the battle became central to Serbian national memory.
After an eight-month search, the journalist Henry Morton Stanley found the missionary at Ujiji on Lake Tanganyika and greeted him, he later claimed, with 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?'

event: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal
note: Guglielmo Marconi heard the Morse letter 'S', sent from Poldhu in Cornwall, on a receiver at Signal Hill above St John's, Newfoundland, its aerial held aloft by a kite.

event: The golden spike completes the first transcontinental railroad
note: Leland Stanford drove a ceremonial golden spike where the Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines met at Promontory Summit in Utah.

The British drove the colonial militia from Breed's Hill on the Charlestown peninsula, across the river from Boston, at a cost of more than 1,000 casualties; the battle took its name from neighbouring Bunker Hill.
A Zulu army of some 20,000 overwhelmed a British camp beneath the sphinx-shaped hill of Isandlwana, the worst defeat of a British army by an indigenous force.
Cook was killed in a skirmish on the shore of Kealakekua Bay, on the Kona coast of Hawaii's Big Island, after trying to take a chief hostage over a stolen boat.
Napoleon's bloodiest battle was fought about 120 km west of Moscow; the Russians withdrew after losing some 45,000 men, and Napoleon entered Moscow a week later.

event: Argentina surrenders, ending the Falklands War
note: Once British troops had taken the mountains ringing the islands' capital, the Argentine commander surrendered his garrison of about 9,800 men at Stanley.

The bloodiest single day in American history: some 23,000 casualties near Sharpsburg, Maryland, as McClellan checked Lee's first invasion of the North, giving Lincoln his opening to announce emancipation.

event: The emperor Akbar founds Fatehpur Sikri
note: Akbar built a new red-sandstone capital at Sikri, west of Agra, honouring a Sufi saint who had foretold the birth of his son; it was largely abandoned after about 14 years.

event: Mexico defeats the French at Puebla
note: General Ignacio Zaragoza's army repelled a French assault on the hill forts of Loreto and Guadalupe above Puebla, a victory remembered as Cinco de Mayo; the French took the city a year later.

event: Sepoys mutiny, sparking the Indian Rebellion
note: Sepoys at the Meerut cantonment, north-east of Delhi, rose after comrades were jailed for refusing cartridges rumoured to be greased with animal fat, then marched on Delhi.

event: China signs the treaty ending the First Opium War
note: The treaty was signed aboard HMS Cornwallis on the Yangtze at Nanjing; China ceded Hong Kong Island and opened five ports to British trade.

event: Operation Market Garden fails at the 'bridge too far'
note: Allied airborne troops tried to seize a chain of Dutch bridges; British paratroops held the north end of the Rhine bridge at Arnhem for four days before being overwhelmed.

event: Vikings raid the monastery on Lindisfarne
note: Norse raiders sacked the monastery on Holy Island off the Northumbrian coast, an attack usually taken as the start of the Viking Age in Britain.

event: Norse explorers camp in North America
note: The only confirmed Norse site in the Americas lies at the northern tip of Newfoundland; tree rings show the Vikings were cutting wood there in 1021.

event: Great Zimbabwe rises in southern Africa
note: The stone city near modern Masvingo was the capital of a kingdom that traded gold and ivory to the Swahili coast; its Great Enclosure is the largest ancient structure south of the Sahara.

event: The Maya build El Castillo at Chichén Itzá
note: The stepped temple to the feathered serpent Kukulcán stands in the Yucatán; at the equinoxes, the light makes a shadow serpent crawl down its northern stair.
The Nazca people scraped hundreds of lines and giant animal figures into the desert plateau of southern Peru, between the towns of Nazca and Palpa; they are best seen from the air.
Emperor Constantine summoned the first ecumenical council of bishops to Nicaea (modern İznik), south-east of Constantinople; it produced the Nicene Creed.
US Marines seized the airfield the Japanese were building on Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands; six months of fighting on land and sea ended with Japan's withdrawal.
Carrier aircraft from the force that had struck Pearl Harbor bombed the port of Darwin, the first and heaviest of almost 100 air raids on northern Australia.
Kitchener's Anglo-Egyptian army, armed with Maxim guns, destroyed the Mahdist army on the plain north of Omdurman, opposite Khartoum; the young Winston Churchill rode in the cavalry charge.
The Abbasid victory over a Tang Chinese army by the Talas River marked the western limit of Chinese power in Central Asia. The exact field is unknown, but it lay near modern Taraz and Talas.

Robert Clive's East India Company army defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Palashi on the Bhagirathi, north of Calcutta, after bribing the Nawab's commander, Mir Jafar: the start of British rule in India.

event: Babur defeats the Sultan of Delhi
note: Babur's smaller army, using field guns and flanking cavalry, killed Sultan Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat, north of Delhi, and founded the Mughal Empire.
The largest land battle of the Persian Wars was fought below the town of Plataea in Boeotia; the Spartan-led Greek army killed Mardonius and ended the Persian invasion of Greece.
Alexander broke Darius III's huge army on a plain in northern Mesopotamia, probably near Tel Gomel north-east of Mosul, opening Babylon and Persia to the Macedonians.
Germanic tribes under Arminius ambushed Varus's army in the Teutoburg Forest; finds since 1987 place the main fighting at Kalkriese, north of Osnabrück.
Scipio Africanus defeated Hannibal in what is now northern Tunisia, ending the Second Punic War; the battlefield, somewhere near Zama Regia, has never been located.

event: Saladin destroys the crusader army at Hattin
note: Saladin trapped the thirsty crusader army on the twin peaks of an extinct volcano west of the Sea of Galilee; three months later he took Jerusalem.

event: The Mamluks halt the Mongols at Ain Jalut
note: The Mamluks of Egypt under Qutuz and Baybars defeated a Mongol army at the spring of Goliath in the Jezreel Valley, stopping the Mongol advance into the Levant and Africa.
The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeated and captured the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV north of Lake Van, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

event: Japan annihilates the Russian fleet at Tsushima
note: Admiral Togo's fleet destroyed the Russian Baltic Fleet, which had sailed halfway round the world, in the strait between Korea and Japan; Russia soon sued for peace.
About 150 British soldiers, many sick or wounded, held a mission station on the Buffalo River against some 4,000 Zulus; eleven of the defenders won the Victoria Cross.
Emperor Menelik II's army routed an Italian invasion force in the mountains of Tigray, preserving Ethiopia's independence through the age of European empire in Africa.
Fletcher Christian's mutineers set Captain Bligh and 18 loyal men adrift near Tofua in Tonga; Bligh sailed the open launch 6,700 km to Timor, while the mutineers hid on Pitcairn Island.
Sam Houston's Texians surprised Santa Anna's army during its afternoon rest beside the San Jacinto River, east of modern Houston, winning Texas its independence in 18 minutes.
Antonio José de Sucre's army defeated the last great royalist army on the plain of Quinua in the Peruvian Andes, sealing South America's independence from Spain.
Simón Bolívar's army, fresh from crossing the Andes, defeated the Spanish at a bridge south of Tunja; three days later he entered Bogotá.

event: Pizarro captures the Inca emperor Atahualpa
note: Francisco Pizarro's 168 Spaniards ambushed Atahualpa's retinue in the main square of the Andean town of Cajamarca and took the emperor hostage.

event: Mao's Long March comes to an end
note: After a fighting retreat of about 10,000 km from Jiangxi, Mao's First Front Army reached the communist base at Wuqi in northern Shaanxi with perhaps a tenth of the men who set out.

event: The first atomic bomb is tested
note: The world's first nuclear explosion, a plutonium device, lit up the Jornada del Muerto desert in New Mexico before dawn, about 55 km south-east of Socorro.
Donald Johanson and Tom Gray found the 3.2-million-year-old skeleton of an Australopithecus afarensis at Hadar in Ethiopia's Afar region; she was named after a Beatles song.

event: An Anglo-Saxon ship burial is unearthed
note: Excavators uncovered the imprint of a 27 m ship, packed with treasures including a famous helmet, in a burial mound at Sutton Hoo near Woodbridge in Suffolk; it is probably the grave of King Rædwald.
Monks Mound, the largest earthwork in pre-Columbian America, stood at the heart of the Mississippian city of Cahokia, across the Mississippi from modern St Louis.

event: 'Bloody Sunday' on the march from Selma
note: State troopers beat civil rights marchers, among them John Lewis, at the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama; the outcry helped pass the Voting Rights Act.

event: Harold II defeats the Norwegian invasion
note: Harold Godwinson surprised and killed Harald Hardrada of Norway at Stamford Bridge, east of York; three days later William landed in Sussex, and Harold had to march south to Hastings.

event: Richard III is killed at Bosworth Field
note: Henry Tudor's victory, in which Richard III became the last English king to die in battle, ended the Wars of the Roses; finds since 2009 place the fighting about 3 km south-west of the traditional site.
Marlborough and Prince Eugene destroyed a Franco-Bavarian army beside the Danube at Blindheim (Blenheim) in Bavaria, saving Vienna; Blenheim Palace was the nation's reward to Marlborough.

event: Peter the Great defeats Sweden at Poltava
note: Peter the Great's army destroyed Charles XII's Swedish army outside the Ukrainian town of Poltava, ending Sweden's time as a great power.
British and Indian troops held a ridge in the Naga Hills, at one point fighting across the district commissioner's tennis court, and helped halt the Japanese invasion of India.
The world's first artificial satellite was launched from Tyuratam (later Baikonur) on the steppe of Soviet Kazakhstan; its radio beeps could be picked up around the world.
An asteroid or comet fragment exploded in the air over the Siberian taiga near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River, flattening some 80 million trees over 2,150 km².
The largest eruption in recorded history, on the island of Sumbawa in Indonesia, killed tens of thousands and caused the 'Year Without a Summer' across the northern hemisphere in 1816.
Mary Leakey found the skull of Paranthropus boisei in Olduvai Gorge, on the edge of the Serengeti in Tanzania, putting East Africa at the centre of the search for human origins.

event: The stone circles of Göbekli Tepe are raised
note: Hunter-gatherers raised rings of carved, T-shaped limestone pillars on a hilltop near Şanlıurfa in south-east Turkey, some 6,000 years before Stonehenge.

event: The last stand of the samurai
note: Saigō Takamori and his last few hundred samurai were overwhelmed by the new conscript army on Shiroyama hill above Kagoshima, ending the Satsuma Rebellion.

event: The Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years' War
note: The treaties were negotiated in the Westphalian towns of Münster and Osnabrück and signed in Münster, whose town hall still has its Hall of Peace.

event: Martin Luther refuses to recant before the emperor
note: At the imperial diet in Worms on the Rhine, Luther refused to disown his writings before Charles V; declared an outlaw, he was spirited away to the Wartburg castle.

event: Andrew Jackson repels a British assault
note: Jackson's mix of regulars, militia, free Black volunteers and pirates beat off a British attack at Chalmette, just below New Orleans, unaware that peace had been signed two weeks earlier.
US 7th Cavalry troops killed some 250 Lakota men, women and children while disarming Spotted Elk's band beside Wounded Knee Creek on the Pine Ridge Reservation, South Dakota.
Antonio José de Sucre's army defeated the Spanish on the slopes of the Pichincha volcano above Quito, freeing what is now Ecuador.

event: Spain and Portugal sign the Treaty of Tordesillas
note: The two crowns split newly charted lands along a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands. The treaty was signed in this Castilian town on the Douro, near Valladolid.
Sun Quan and Liu Bei's allied fleet used fire ships to rout Cao Cao on the Yangtze, ensuring China split into three kingdoms; the most widely accepted site is the cliffs at Chibi in Hubei.

event: Admiral Yi's victory at Hansan Island
note: Yi Sun-sin lured a Japanese fleet out of a narrow strait and destroyed it off Hansan Island in a 'crane wing' formation, cutting Japan's sea supply line during its invasion of Korea.
Julius Caesar beat Pompey's larger army on the plain beside the Enipeus river near Pharsalus in Thessaly; Pompey fled to Egypt, where he was murdered.

event: Parthian horse archers destroy Crassus's legions
note: Parthian cavalry shot Marcus Licinius Crassus's army to pieces on the open plain near Carrhae (Harran) in what is now south-east Turkey; Crassus was killed during truce talks.

event: The Goths kill Emperor Valens in battle
note: Gothic warriors destroyed the eastern Roman field army outside Adrianople (Edirne) in Thrace and killed the emperor Valens: a turning point in Rome's struggle with the barbarians.

event: Aetius checks Attila on the Catalaunian Plains
note: A Roman and Visigothic army under Flavius Aetius halted Attila's Huns in Champagne. The exact battlefield is unknown, somewhere between Troyes and Châlons-en-Champagne.
Arab Muslim armies under Khalid ibn al-Walid routed the Byzantines by the Yarmouk river, south-east of the Sea of Galilee, ending Byzantine rule in Syria.

event: Otto the Great defeats the Magyars
note: Otto I's German army crushed the Hungarian raiders on the Lech floodplain near Augsburg, ending decades of Magyar raids into western Europe.

event: Suleiman the Magnificent crushes Hungary at Mohács
note: The Ottoman army destroyed the Hungarian army on the Danube plain south of Mohács; King Louis II drowned in flight, and Hungary was carved up for 150 years.

event: Voortrekkers defeat the Zulu army at Blood River
note: About 470 Voortrekkers in a laager of 64 wagons beside the Ncome River repulsed a Zulu army of some 15,000; three Boers were wounded and about 3,000 Zulus killed.
Cuban and Angolan troops held the town against South African and UNITA forces in Africa's largest battle since the Second World War; the stalemate led to Namibian independence.

event: British forces capture the fortress of Louisbourg
note: Amherst and Wolfe took France's great fortress on Cape Breton Island after a seven-week siege, opening the St Lawrence for the attack on Quebec.
William Henry Harrison's troops repulsed an attack by warriors of Tecumseh's confederacy near Prophetstown in Indiana; 'Tippecanoe and Tyler too' later helped win him the presidency.

event: A Vodou ceremony launches the Haitian Revolution
note: Enslaved leaders met in a forest clearing near Cap-Français (Cap-Haïtien), traditionally at Bois Caïman, where Dutty Boukman called for the revolt that became the Haitian Revolution.

event: San Martín wins the Battle of Maipú
note: José de San Martín's army defeated the royalists on the plain of Maipú, south-west of Santiago, securing Chile's independence.

event: Chilean troops storm the Morro of Arica
note: In the War of the Pacific, Chilean infantry took the fortified headland above the port of Arica in under an hour; the city has been Chilean ever since.
King Oswiu of Northumbria chose Roman rather than Irish custom for dating Easter at a council in Abbess Hild's monastery on the Yorkshire coast.

event: Pope Urban II calls for the First Crusade
note: At the end of a church council at Clermont in the Auvergne, Urban II preached to a crowd in a field outside the city, which answered 'Deus vult!' (God wills it).
Kitchener confronted Captain Marchand's small French expedition at the ruined fort of Fashoda on the White Nile; France backed down, and Sudan stayed under British control.

event: Yuri Gagarin lands after the first human spaceflight
note: Gagarin ejected from Vostok 1 and parachuted into a field near Engels in the Saratov region; a farmer and her granddaughter were the first to greet him.

event: Burke and Wills reach the northern coast of Australia
note: Robert O'Hara Burke and William Wills reached the tidal mangroves near the Gulf of Carpentaria, completing the first south-to-north crossing of Australia; both died on the way back.

event: Çatalhöyük, one of the first towns, is founded
note: One of the world's earliest towns grew on the Konya plain in central Anatolia; its people entered their mud-brick houses through the roof and buried their dead beneath the floors.

event: Australians hold the Kokoda Track at Isurava
note: Outnumbered Australian militia and AIF battalions fought a Japanese force in the Owen Stanley Range at Isurava, a key stand in the defence of Port Moresby.
The largest land battle before 1914 was fought outside Mukden (Shenyang) in Manchuria; Japan's victory over Russia came at enormous cost to both sides.
Prussia's victory near the Bohemian village of Sadová (Sadowa), north-west of Königgrätz (Hradec Králové), settled which power would unite Germany.
British and Indian forces besieged in the Manipur valley around Imphal held out until the Japanese offensive collapsed, in what was later voted Britain's greatest battle.

event: Dmitry Donskoy defeats the Golden Horde
note: Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow defeated the Tatar commander Mamai on the Kulikovo Field near the upper Don, south of Tula, a symbol of Russia's rise against the Horde.
Alexander Nevsky's Novgorodians defeated the Teutonic Knights on the frozen Lake Peipus, between modern Estonia and Russia; the exact spot on the lake is unknown.
A Polish–Lithuanian army under Władysław II Jagiełło crushed the Teutonic Knights between the villages of Grunwald and Stębark in Prussia, one of medieval Europe's largest battles.
Quarrymen near Taung in South Africa found the skull of a young child that Raymond Dart named Australopithecus africanus, the first early human ancestor found in Africa.
Robert Baden-Powell's garrison held the railway town of Mafeking for 217 days against the Boers; news of its relief set off wild celebrations in Britain.

event: Mexico cedes California to the United States
note: Mexico gave up about half its territory in a treaty signed at Guadalupe Hidalgo, beside the great shrine just north of Mexico City.

event: Ramesses II fights the Hittites at Kadesh
note: Probably the largest chariot battle ever fought, on the Orontes River in western Syria. Both sides claimed victory, and it led to one of the earliest surviving peace treaties; the city's site is Tell Nebi Mend.
Alexander crossed the swollen Jhelum (Hydaspes) in a storm and defeated Porus and his war elephants in the Punjab; the crossing point, probably near Jalalpur, is disputed.

The Mauryan emperor's conquest of Kalinga, on India's east coast, was so bloody that he renounced war and turned to Buddhism; his edicts are carved on a rock at Dhauli, near the traditional battlefield.

event: Tipu Sultan dies defending his capital
note: British troops stormed Tipu Sultan's island fortress of Seringapatam in the Kaveri river near Mysore; Tipu was killed fighting at the breach.

event: A typhoon wrecks Kublai Khan's invasion fleet
note: The 'kamikaze', or divine wind, destroyed the Mongol fleet sheltering off Takashima island in Imari Bay, Kyushu, where archaeologists have since found its wrecks.

event: The Knights of St John withstand a great Ottoman siege
note: In the Great Siege of Malta, the Knights and the Maltese held Birgu and Fort St Angelo for four months against a huge Ottoman force; Valletta was built across the Grand Harbour afterwards.

event: Nelson destroys Napoleon's fleet at anchor
note: At the Battle of the Nile, Nelson caught the French fleet in Aboukir Bay, east of Alexandria, and destroyed it; the flagship L'Orient blew up, stranding Bonaparte's army in Egypt.

event: Epaminondas's oblique attack breaks the Spartans
note: The Thebans massed their left wing 50 ranks deep and shattered the Spartan army at Leuctra in Boeotia, ending Sparta's dominance of Greece; the battle trophy's base survives.

event: Rome defeats the Macedonian phalanx at Pydna
note: The legions of Lucius Aemilius Paullus broke King Perseus's phalanx on uneven ground near Pydna, below Mount Olympus, ending the Macedonian kingdom.

event: Scipio starves out the Celtiberians of Numantia
note: Scipio Aemilianus ringed the hill town with 9 km of walls and starved it out after twenty years of resistance; many defenders chose death over surrender. Its ruins lie near Soria.

event: Pelagius defeats the Umayyads at Covadonga
note: A small Asturian force under Pelagius (Pelayo) beat an Umayyad detachment in a valley of the Picos de Europa, traditionally the beginning of the Christian Reconquista.
Basques ambushed the rearguard of Charlemagne's army in a pass in the western Pyrenees, killing Roland, whose death became the subject of the Song of Roland.

event: Flemish militias defeat the French knights
note: The town militias of Flanders routed the French chivalry by a stream outside Kortrijk (Courtrai) and hung hundreds of captured golden spurs in a church.
John I of Portugal and his English archers defeated a much larger Castilian army near Aljubarrota, securing Portugal's independence; the monastery of Batalha was built in thanks.

event: James IV of Scotland is killed at Flodden
note: James IV, invading England in support of France, was killed with much of his nobility by an English army at Branxton in Northumberland: the last British monarch to die in battle.

event: The Andean rebel Túpac Amaru II is executed
note: After leading the largest rising against Spanish rule in the Andes, José Gabriel Condorcanqui was executed, with his wife Micaela Bastidas, in the main square of Cusco, the old Inca capital.

event: Edward Jenner gives the first vaccination
note: Country doctor Edward Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with cowpox at Berkeley in Gloucestershire, then showed that the boy was immune to smallpox.

event: Tycho Brahe builds his observatory, Uraniborg
note: Granted the island of Hven in the Øresund by King Frederick II of Denmark, Tycho built the most advanced observatory in pre-telescope Europe there.

event: Three leaders sign the accords dissolving the USSR
note: The leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus met at a government hunting lodge at Viskuli in the Białowieża Forest, by the Polish border, and declared that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist.

event: Thutmose III defeats the Canaanite kings
note: The pharaoh surprised a Canaanite coalition by marching through a narrow pass to the city of Megiddo, then besieged it for seven months: the first battle recorded in detail. Megiddo gave its name to Armageddon.

event: Shalmaneser III fights a coalition including King Ahab
note: The Assyrian king fought twelve allied kings, among them Ahab of Israel, at Qarqar on the Orontes in north-west Syria, probably Tell Qarqur; his inscription is the first record of camels in battle.
Qin defeated the state of Zhao near modern Gaoping in Shanxi after a long stand-off and reportedly buried the surrendered Zhao army alive, clearing its path to unify China.

event: Maharana Pratap fights the Mughals at Haldighati
note: The ruler of Mewar fought Akbar's army under Man Singh in a narrow pass in the Aravalli hills, north of Udaipur; though he lost the field, he became a hero of Rajput resistance.

event: Arthur Wellesley defeats the Marathas at Assaye
note: The future Duke of Wellington beat a far larger Maratha army where two rivers meet in the Deccan, north-east of Aurangabad; he later called it the best thing he ever did in the fighting way.
A small British and Indian garrison held the fort of Chitral, deep in the Hindu Kush, for about seven weeks until relief columns fought their way over the mountain passes.

event: Nobunaga's musketeers break the Takeda cavalry
note: Oda Nobunaga's arquebusiers, firing from behind wooden palisades, cut down the famous Takeda horsemen on the plain of Shitaragahara near Nagashino Castle.

event: The Minamoto destroy the Taira fleet
note: The Minamoto clan defeated the Taira at sea in the narrow Kanmon Strait between Honshu and Kyushu; the child emperor Antoku drowned, and the Kamakura shogunate followed.

event: Tran Hung Dao traps a Mongol fleet on stakes
note: The Vietnamese general lured a Yuan Mongol fleet over iron-tipped stakes driven into the Bach Dang estuary near Ha Long Bay; as the tide fell, the ships were impaled and destroyed.

event: Zhukov defeats Japan on the Mongolian border
note: Soviet and Mongolian forces under Georgy Zhukov encircled the Japanese army on the Khalkhin Gol river on the Manchurian border; Japan then turned its ambitions south.

event: The first skull of 'Peking Man' is found
note: Pei Wenzhong found a Homo erectus skullcap in a limestone cave at Zhoukoudian, about 50 km south-west of Beijing; most of the fossils vanished in 1941.

event: Russia and Qing China sign their first treaty
note: Envoys met at the Russian fort of Nerchinsk in eastern Siberia and fixed the border along the Argun river and the Stanovoy mountains, with Jesuit priests interpreting in Latin.
After a night march across the desert, Wolseley's army stormed Urabi Pasha's trenches at Tel el-Kebir, between Cairo and the Suez Canal, beginning Britain's long occupation of Egypt.
Boer commandos scaled the steep hill on the Natal border and routed the British force on its summit, winning the First Boer War.

event: Ras Alula destroys an Italian column
note: Ethiopian troops destroyed an Italian column marching to relieve a fort inland from Massawa, on the Red Sea coast of what is now Eritrea.

event: The golden rhinoceros is buried at Mapungubwe
note: Mapungubwe, by the meeting of the Limpopo and Shashe rivers, was the capital of southern Africa's first great kingdom; a gold-foil rhinoceros from a royal grave on its hill was found in 1933.

event: The Battle of the Three Kings
note: King Sebastian of Portugal's crusade into Morocco ended in disaster by the Loukkos river near Ksar el-Kebir; he and both rival Moroccan sultans died, and Portugal soon fell to Spain.

event: Farmers find the Gnostic Gospels in Upper Egypt
note: A farmer digging for fertiliser below the Jabal al-Tarif cliffs near Nag Hammadi found a jar holding thirteen leather-bound codices, including the Gospel of Thomas.

event: Andrew Jackson crushes the Red Stick Creeks
note: Jackson's army, with Cherokee and Lower Creek allies, stormed the Red Sticks' fortified bend of the Tallapoosa River in Alabama, ending the Creek War.

event: Paraguay repels the Triple Alliance at Curupayty
note: Paraguayan troops behind a trench line by the Paraguay River cut down an assault by Brazil and Argentina, the Allies' worst defeat of the War of the Triple Alliance.
Jean-Jacques Dessalines's army took the French forts ringing Cap-Français, forcing Rochambeau to evacuate; Haiti declared independence six weeks later.
After a 1,900 km fighting retreat, Chief Joseph of the Nez Perce surrendered in the Bear Paw Mountains of Montana, about 65 km from the Canadian border: 'I will fight no more forever.'

event: Isaac Brock dies repelling an American invasion
note: British regulars, Canadian militia and Mohawk warriors threw back an American invasion across the Niagara River; General Isaac Brock was killed leading a charge up Queenston Heights.

Colorado volunteers under John Chivington attacked a peaceful Cheyenne and Arapaho camp on Sand Creek in eastern Colorado, killing well over a hundred people, most of them women, children and the elderly.

event: Australians defeat a Japanese landing at Milne Bay
note: Australian troops beat off a Japanese landing at the head of Milne Bay, on the eastern tip of New Guinea: the first time Japanese forces were decisively defeated on land in the war.
US Marines and soldiers spent ten weeks taking a small coral island in Palau from Japanese defenders dug into limestone caves, one of the costliest battles of the Pacific war.

event: Shackleton's Endurance sinks in the ice
note: Crushed by pack ice in the Weddell Sea, Shackleton's ship sank off Antarctica; all 28 men survived after an epic journey. The wreck was found in 2022, 3,000 m down.
Sponge divers off the small Greek island of Antikythera, between Crete and the Peloponnese, raised objects from a Roman-era wreck, among them a corroded geared astronomical calculator.
